questions.question: What was Valli's favourite pastime?
answer_steps: Standing at the front door watching the street.
Above all, watching the bus that went between her village and the town.

questions.question: What was a source of unending joy for Valli? What was her deepest desire?
answer_steps: Watching the bus and the new set of passengers each time.
Her deepest desire was to ride on that bus.

questions.question: What did Valli find out about the bus journey? How did she find out these details?
answer_steps: The town was six miles away, the fare was thirty paise one way and the trip took forty-five minutes.
She listened to neighbours and asked discreet questions.

questions.question: Why did the conductor call Valli 'Madam'?
answer_steps: She spoke and behaved like a grown-up lady.
She insisted on doing everything herself, so he teased her playfully.

questions.question: Why didn't Valli want to make friends with the elderly woman?
answer_steps: She found the woman ugly, with ear lobes stretched by heavy earrings, and chewing betel.
She disliked being treated as a child; she said she could take care of herself.

questions.question: Why didn't Valli get off the bus at the bus station in the town?
answer_steps: She had money only for the return fare.
So she stayed in the bus and returned by it.

questions.question: Why didn't Valli want to go to the stall and have a drink? What does this tell you about her?
answer_steps: She had no money for it and would not accept a free drink.
It shows she was proud and independent and did not want charity.

questions.question: What happened on the return journey that saddened Valli?
answer_steps: She saw the young cow, which had run before the bus earlier, lying dead by the roadside.
It had been hit by a vehicle; the sight took away all her joy.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*Valli stood at the front doorway of her house, looking out at what was happening in the street.*
*There were no playmates of her age on her street, and this was about all she had to do.*

(i) How old was Valli?

(ii) Where was she standing?

(iii) Why did she spend time watching the street?

(iv) What on the street interested her most?

(v) Give a word from the story meaning 'hobby'.
answer_steps: (i) Eight.
(ii) At the front doorway of her house.
(iii) She had no playmates of her age there.
(iv) The bus to the town.
(v) Pastime.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*'Stand back, stand back,' said the conductor. 'Here comes a madam.'*
*Valli did not like being called 'madam' by him, and she said, 'I'm not a madam.'*

(i) Who calls Valli 'madam'?

(ii) Why does he call her that?

(iii) What tone does he use?

(iv) What does Valli's reply show?

(v) Who is the 'madam' in the title of the story?
answer_steps: (i) The bus conductor.
(ii) She acts like a grown-up lady; he is teasing her.
(iii) Playful, joking.
(iv) She is independent and self-respecting.
(v) Valli.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*It was the same young cow, lying dead by the roadside, just where it had been struck by some passing vehicle.*
*Valli no longer wanted to look out of the window.*

(i) Which cow is meant?

(ii) How had it died?

(iii) How did Valli feel?

(iv) Why did she not want to look out now?

(v) What contrast does this create?
answer_steps: (i) The young cow that had run in front of the bus earlier.
(ii) It was hit by a passing vehicle.
(iii) Sad and frightened.
(iv) The sight of death took away her joy.
(v) Joy on the way to town, sorrow on the way back.

questions.question: How did Valli plan her journey?
answer_steps: She found out the fare, distance and time by listening and asking discreet questions.
She saved sixty paise and chose her mother's nap time so no one would miss her.

questions.question: Write a character sketch of Valli.
answer_steps: Valli is curious: she watches the bus every day and asks questions.
She is determined: she saves sixty paise by giving up treats.
She is independent and proud: she pays her own fare and refuses help, friendship and charity.
She is practical: she stays on the bus as she has only the return fare.
She is sensitive: the dead cow saddens her; her trip teaches her about life and death.
marking_scheme: 3 marks: content (relevant points from the text)

questions.question: How does the outward journey differ from the return journey? What does this teach Valli?
answer_steps: Going, Valli is thrilled: she enjoys the canal, palm trees, mountains and laughs at the running cow.
Returning, she sees the same cow dead and loses all interest in the view.
The contrast moves the story from joy to sorrow.
Valli learns that life includes death and loss, and she grows up a little.
marking_scheme: 3 marks: content (relevant points from the text)

questions.question: What did Valli see on the way to the town?
answer_steps: A canal, palm trees, grassland, distant mountains and the blue sky.
A young cow running in front of the bus with its tail up, which made her laugh.

questions.question: How did the conductor treat Valli? How did she respond?
answer_steps: He teased her kindly, called her 'Madam' and offered her a drink.
She answered with dignity, refused help and the drink, and insisted she was not a child.

questions.question: Why did Valli choose the afternoon for her trip?
answer_steps: Her mother usually took a nap from one to four.
She could go and return before her mother woke up.

questions.question: How is the dead cow a turning point in the story?
answer_steps: On the way out the cow made Valli laugh; on the way back it lay dead.
Her joy turned to sorrow and she learnt about death for the first time.

The conductor's teasing, the elderly woman, the views and the running cow.
Staying on the bus at the town; the dead cow on the way back.
Your feelings: pride, joy, then sadness; keeping the secret.
